description: Replace the logins of a connected mailbox: SMTP and IMAP, or SMTP alone for a send-only mailbox, which answers 400 if `imap` is sent. We sign in with each first, and nothing changes if one fails. It changes how we sign in, nothing else: it copies no mail between servers and changes no DNS record. While a copy of this mailbox's old mail to our servers runs, the IMAP login can move only to the copy's new mailbox, at its switch (get_mailbox_migration's `next.reason` is `owner_switch`), with SMTP moving there too; any other new IMAP server answers 409. From that switch until our team copies the last mail, nothing sends from the mailbox. A mailbox that signs in with Microsoft or Google has no logins here and answers 409: a signed-in owner signs it in again, and an API key asks for that with create_handoff (kind update_mailbox_credentials, with its mailboxId). Leave `handoffId` out with an API key: it is for the console, and a key that sends it gets 400. It needs setup permission. A signed-in owner has it and can give it to an API key for the whole workspace. That key loses it if its maker stops being the owner.

expectedImapSourceId.description: Only update an SMTP/IMAP mailbox if its imapSourceId still matches this value. null means the original source. A mismatch answers 409: read the mailbox again before retrying. Leave this field out for other providers.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

imap.description: Required for a mailbox that sends and receives. Leave it out for a send-only mailbox, which has no IMAP login.

name: update_mailbox_credentials
title: Update mailbox logins
